prerequisites: Physics (high density energy source, heat transfer, phase changes)
Manufacturing technologies 1 and 2 (metal material removal and joining processes, characteristics of cutting and joining processes)

learning_outcomes.text: Explain the principles, potential and limitations of additive manufacturing technologies
Understand the complete AM production chain from digital design and simulation to final part realization
Understand metal additive manufacturing systems, processes, and key quality considerations
Evaluate AM process selection and cost-effectiveness for industrial

syllabus_topics: Basic physical principles of AM of metals
Properties of materials for AM and incoming material quality control
Physical basics of high density energy sources and defects in AM
DED -Arc path generation, process control and applications
Basics of laser light metal interactions
DED-LB/M wire systems, process and AM applications
DED-LB/M powder systems, process and AM applications
PBF-LB/M systems, process and AM applications
Laser based AM of multi and functionally graded materials
bibliography: E. Govekar, A Jeromen Lecture Notes: Laser Based Additive Manufacturing Processes
D. Klobčar, U. Trdan: Lecture notes for Additive technologies.
U. Trdan, D. Klobčar: Tutorial notes for Additive technologies.
Linkan Bian, Nima Shamsaei, and John M. Usher: Laser-Based Additive Manufacturing of Metal Parts: Modeling, Optimization, and Control of Mechanical Properties, 2018
O. Diegel, A. Nordin, D. Motte: A Practical Guide to Design for Additive Manufacturing, Springler series in Advanced Manufacturing, 2020
degree: Mechanical Engineering (2nd cycle, Erasmus+ subjects, Research and Development programme)
